title: A class-level template type argument substitutes into the member's return type

ground_truth.statement: Box declares @template T with @return T on get(), so the annotation @param Box<Cat> tells the caller that get() hands back a Cat, and the member access that follows has to be resolved against Cat - which has no bark(). The runtime script decides both halves independently of any analyzer: a value taken from a Box<Dog> dispatches Dog::bark() and returns 'woof', a value taken from a Box<Cat> dispatches Cat::meow() and returns 'meow' (so the substituted type is the class the annotation names, not mixed), and the same get()->bark() access on the Box<Cat> side fails with 'Error: Call to undefined method Cat::bark()'. Callers cannot weaken this: the class-level template is part of the annotation the callee published, exactly like a native parameter type.

notes: The rule under test is template substitution into a member's type at a use site: the same member access, on the same generic class, with only the type argument changed. All three tools substitute and report, under their own code: PHPStan 2.3.1 method.notFound, Psalm 6.20.0 UndefinedMethod, Mago 1.57.0 non-existent-method. The two forbidden predicates are the asymmetric controls and they are what makes the row about substitution rather than about member access: line 41 is the identical get()->bark() on Box<Dog>, which must stay silent, and line 53 is get()->meow() on Box<Cat>, which must stay silent too. The second control is the harder one - a tool that treated the declared @return mixed of get() as the receiver would report meow() as undefined on mixed and fail the case - so a tool cannot pass by guessing. The required predicates also pin the substituted class in the message ('Cat::bark' / 'bark ... Cat'), so an undefined-method report that does not name Cat does not satisfy the case. Every diagnostic the three tools produced is claimed by a predicate; nothing is acknowledged away and nothing is widened. No existing case in this corpus uses an undefined-method rule class, and none of the other generics cases covers member resolution on a substituted type argument (they cover inference from an argument and a declared bound). The round's source material, Mago's analyzer test suite, is a directory of fixtures without catalogue candidate IDs, and no catalogue lead covers this rule, so no source_candidate_id is recorded.

sources.note: pattern source for the class-level @template T with @return T on get(); that fixture consumes the substituted value as a scalar (invalid-argument), this one resolves a member on it. Rewritten, not copied.

further evidence that the class-level type argument is substituted into member signatures in this dialect; no case in the suite expects a non-existent-method from that substitution, so Mago is judged by the runtime proof here, like the other two tools
